Article Title: ‘Congress has not had a level playing field’: Sonia targets Modi govt amid SIR row
Article Text:
Sonia Gandhi said she was not pessimistic about the Congress party's future.

'I'm not so pessimistic'

Sonia PM on Modi, RSS and Manmohan Singh

NEW DELHI: Congress leader Sonia Gandhi has alleged that her party and other opposition parties have not had a level playing field since the BJP came to power in 2014, accusing the Modi government of exercising control over key institutions, including the Election Commission In an interview with The Hindu ahead of the November 10 release of her memoir, "Belonging: A Journey of Love", the former Congress president said the Congress had continued to fight despite what she described as institutional pressure, control over mainstream media and the use of money and religion in politics.Her remarks come amid the opposition's campaign against the Election Commission over the ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.The Congress-led INDIA bloc held a major rally at Delhi's Ramlila Maidan on November 1, accusing the poll body of electoral irregularities and demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.The Opposition has alleged that the revision exercise could lead to eligible voters being removed from electoral rolls. The Congress has also stepped up its criticism of the Election Commission and its handling of the process.Asked about the Congress's decline, its present position and its prospects, Sonia said she was not pessimistic about the party's future. She argued that the Congress and other opposition parties had been operating under difficult conditions since the BJP came to power."I am not so pessimistic. Consider that the Congress party and other opposition parties have not had a level playing field since this government came to power. Take into account the complete stranglehold they have on all institutions, especially the Election Commission, their control of mainstream media, their money power and their exploitation of religion."She maintained that the Congress had shown resilience despite these challenges and continued to make progress."Yet, our party is fighting and making progress; in fact, it is the only party that has had the resilience to withstand this onslaught," Gandhi said.She alleged that Congress workers and leaders had faced different forms of persecution but continued to uphold the party's constitutional values."And yet, in every village and every district, Congressmen and women are still fighting for the values enshrined in our Constitution," she said.Gandhi also alleged that several elections had been manipulated and claimed that voters were increasingly aware of it."What is more, it has been amply proved in recent months that many elections have been stolen, and people are now more aware of it," she alleged. "The Congress is working with like-minded parties, and our prospects are improving day by day," she said.The Congress leader also accused the Modi government of weakening India's democratic institutions over the past 12 years, warning that rebuilding them would take considerable time even after a change in government."Over the last twelve years great damage has been done to the fabric of our country, our democracy and our institutions. Even after this government goes, it will take time to restore our systems back to health and great effort from political parties," she said.However, she expressed confidence that people would support a return to what she described as proper governance."But I am optimistic and I know that the people of India will welcome a return to proper governance," the former Congress chief said.Asked what the Congress could learn from Prime Minister Narendra Modi's political rise, Gandhi said his ideological background was different from that of the Congress but dismissed the need for the party to draw lessons from the RSS."It's true that he comes from a very different ideological world. But there are many ways that people succeed in politics within the Congress party, take for example Dr. Manmohan Singh and Congress President Mallikarjun Kharge. I don't think we have much to learn from the RSS."She also rejected the suggestion that she had ever reconsidered her decision to decline the prime minister's post after the Congress-led alliance won the 2004 general election."No, not at all. That has never crossed my mind. Our experience was by and large a very positive one. We worked as a team, and our roles were distinct, with him (Singh) leading the government and I leading the party."Gandhi's 544-page memoir, "Belonging: A Journey of Love", is scheduled to be released in India by HarperCollins India on November 10. The book is primarily a personal account of her life, with political events forming the backdrop to her journey.
Article Summary: Sonia Gandhi says she is not pessimistic about the Congress party's future. She accuses the Modi government of exercising control over key institutions, including the Election Commission. The former Congress president said the Congress had continued to fight despite institutional pressure, control over mainstream media and use of money and religion in politics.

Article Title: 'More you connect with locals, weaker enemy’s plots become': Rajnath Singh's message to troops in WB's Bagdogra

NEW DELHI: Defence minister Rajnath Singh on Saturday addressed soldiers in West Bengal's Bagdogra and advised them to build a deeper connect with local residents in sensitive border areas."The more you connect with local people, the weaker the enemy's plots will become," news agency ANI quoted him as saying."At the post where you serve, your conduct, your uniform, your language and your restraint shape the army's image in the minds of local people. The people of Bagdogra and the surrounding areas have great affection for the army. It is also your responsibility to preserve that affection," he said.Singh underlined the need for discipline and courage, calling them vital qualities for every soldier in the armed forces."No matter how advanced technology is, if our soldiers lack discipline and courage, it is useless. Our armed forces are known for their discipline. Discipline is what transforms an ordinary soldier into an extraordinary warrior. Your discipline is your greatest strength," he said."Among the challenges we face today, morale is the greatest weapon. When your morale is high, you can achieve great victories even with a small team.How does morale grow? Morale grows when you know that your country is with you, your leadership is with you," he added.Bagdogra lies near the strategically significant Siliguri Corridor , popularly known as the 'Chicken's Neck', a narrow strip of land in northern West Bengal that connects mainland India to the northeastern states. The corridor is also in close proximity to the international borders with China, Nepal, Bhutan and Bangladesh.
Article Summary: Rajnath Singh urges soldiers in Bagdogra to strengthen ties with locals in sensitive border areas. Article Title: 'Let Modi, Rahul question each other': Kapil Sibal wants 'historic' debate on SIR
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Senior advocate Kapil Sibal on Saturday questioned the government's changing stand on holding a discussion on the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls in Parliament, suggesting that Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi sit together for an open debate on the issue."Earlier, when the Opposition demanded a discussion on SIR, the Home Minister said the government had nothing to do with it as it was the Election Commission's responsibility. Now, he is saying that a special session can be convened for a discussion. Why has the government's stand changed? I have a suggestion: let the Prime Minister and the Leader of Opposition sit together and question each other. Let the discussion continue as long as possible. This would give the Prime Minister an opportunity to answer questions for the first time in 12 years, which would be a historic occasion," Sibal said.His remarks came after Rahul Gandhi on Saturday challenged Union Home Minister Amit Shah to an open debate on the SIR exercise. Sharing a video of Shah's remarks, the Congress leader said, "Amit Shah ji, don't confuse Modi ji. Just convince him to have an open debate with me.Any platform, any time. Don't be afraid."The challenge drew a sharp response from the BJP, with Parliamentary Affairs Minister Pralhad Joshi accusing Rahul of sharing an edited video of Shah's remarks without the proper context. He said the clip exposed Rahul's "absolute lack of homework on SIR".The video featured Shah's remarks in Parliament and at another public address. In his parliamentary remarks, Shah questioned the possibility of holding a discussion on SIR in the House and asked who would be held responsible if questions were raised.Responding to Rahul's demand for a debate with the Prime Minister, Shah said Modi's presence was not necessary for the discussion."Rahul ji, Modi ji ki zaroorat nahi hai... Hum SIR par charcha ke liye vishesh sansad ka satra bulane ke liye taiyaar hain," Shah said.The edited video juxtaposed Shah's remarks with an earlier statement by Rahul, who had said, "Inko hum matlab pagal kar denge". It ended with Rahul smiling at a press conference, alongside an overlay reading "Confusion mein aa gaye".
Article Summary: Sibal challenges PM Modi and Rahul to sit together for an open debate on SIR. His remarks came after Rahul Gandhi on Saturday challenged Union Home Minister Amit Shah. Article Title: One more chance for excluded voters in Delhi, 6 other states
Article Text:

They won't have to fill form 6, EC says

EC directs BLOs to trace electors through house visits and phone calls

NEW DELHI: Electors across seven states/UTs undergoing SIR, including Delhi, who were excluded from the draft electoral roll on account of being absent, shifted, dead or duplicate (ASDD) and whose enumeration forms (EFs) were not received, will be provided one more opportunity to get their names included in the final electoral roll by filling up the SIR form afresh. They will no longer have to fill Form 6, meant for fresh enrolment, or Form 8, if they were excluded due to shifting of place of residence within the same state/UT.The drive in states where SIR is under way - Delhi, Haryana, Maharashtra, Andhra Pradesh, Jharkhand, Telangana and Nagaland - may come as a relief for deleted electors who were reluctant to fill Form 6 to be added back, in view of the declaration in the form that they were enrolling for the first time. "Basically, the enumeration window which stopped with the publication of draft roll is being reopened for the deleted ASDD voters till the end of the claims and objections period," an EC official said.EC, in a letter to chief electoral officers of the above states/UT, said ASDD electors may submit their EF physically or online to the electoral registration officer or booth-level officer (BLO), along with an annexure mentioning the reason why they could not submit it earlier and declaring that they have not submitted Form 6 for fresh enrolment during SIR.An elector who was excluded due to shifting of residence within the same state/UT can submit the EF along with an annexure mentioning why it was not submitted earlier and declaring that they have not submitted Form 6 during SIR. In the annexure, such voters must mention the address where they were enrolled earlier as well as the address to which they have now shifted. Residence proof will need to be attached.The EF, along with the annexure, must be submitted to the ERO of the assembly constituency to which the voter has shifted. The poll panel said partially filled EFs of left-out ASDD electors will be generated afresh in the ERO dashboard in ECINet. The district election officer and ERO shall make all efforts to contact such electors through BLOs.The district election officer and ERO shall ensure delivery of EFs either physically or electronically via WhatsApp, SMS or email where contact details are available. Affected electors can download and fill up EF on ECINet with their old EPIC number.Booth-wise lists of such ASDD voters will be displayed afresh on notice boards and also uploaded on the CEO's website.EC directed BLOs to get in touch with electors marked as ASDD through house-to-house visits; enquiries from neighbours, family members, RWAs and by using available contact numbers.EFs received from such electors shall be processed and disposed of by EROs concerned after verification of the applicant's eligibility, ordinary residence as well as field verification.Once approved, the same EPIC number assigned to the elector prior to SIR shall be re-assigned. An elector who has already submitted Form 6 for fresh enrolment during SIR need not submit the enumeration form with statement afresh.
Article Summary: Electors excluded from draft electoral roll will be given one more opportunity to get their names included in final electoral roll. They will no longer have to fill Form 6, meant for fresh enrolment, or Form 8, if they were excluded due to shifting of place of residence within state/UT.

Article Title: Ailing Kerala elephant calf, Maya, airlifted to Anant Ambani's Vantara for intensive hospitalisation
Article Text:
A crucial second opinion brings renewed hope

A collaborative model of compassionate care

Maya, an 18-month-old critically ill orphaned elephant calf, has been airlifted from Kerala’s Abhayaranyam to Anant Ambani's Vantara in Jamnagar for specialised intensive hospitalisation. The calf, who has been unable to stand following a severe fall in July, was shifted to the facility after medical experts sought advanced veterinary intervention as a final effort to prevent euthanasia. This life-saving transfer was initiated when Kerala officials explicitly requested the intervention of Vantara to explore every possible medical avenue.Maya's short life has already been a test of resilience. On April 19, 2025, she was found abandoned as a severely dehydrated newborn near Kaprikkad in the Malayattoor Division. Rescued and brought to Abhayaranyam, she was hand-reared around the clock by the Kerala Forest Department. Sadly, her struggles did not end there. On July 2, 2026, the calf slipped while playing and injured her right shoulder. Despite physiotherapy and dietary supplements, her condition rapidly deteriorated.By late October, she could no longer stand and was accepting only liquid feed. A thorough external examination revealed multiple fractures in her limbs, a chest infection, and generalised bone thinning. Faced with extremely brittle bones and a grave prognosis, a Medical Board made the heavy animal-welfare decision to recommend euthanasia on October 29 to prevent further suffering.Refusing to close the case, Kerala’s Chief Wildlife Warden, Dr. P. Pugazhendi, pursued a wider expert opinion before considering any irreversible actions. After reviewing her X-rays and blood work during a video consultation, Vantara’s veterinary experts identified a potential parathyroid-related disorder that could respond to treatment. With this new possibility, the decision was unanimously made on November 5 to transfer Maya to Vantara. At their facility, she will receive comprehensive pain management, advanced diagnostics, and support from hydraulic lifting systems to position her safely. Stepping in to provide this critical care, Vantara acted on the core principle of Anant Ambani: every life matters, driven by the philosophy of Jeev Seva.What makes this medical mission truly remarkable is the deep partnership built around the calf's emotional well-being. Before the journey, Vantara submitted a comprehensive treatment plan, and arranged an airlift equipped with life-support systems. To ensure Maya feels secure in an unfamiliar environment, the Kerala Forest Department has sent Assistant Forest Veterinary Officer Dr. Binoy C. Babu and her familiar caregiver, Shri Nikhil Babu, to accompany her on the flight.Crucially, her caregiver will remain by her side throughout the entire treatment period in Jamnagar to provide vital continuity. A Kerala Monitoring Committee will closely oversee her medical progress, and once the treatment is complete, Vantara will facilitate her return home to Abhayaranyam.The road ahead is undeniably difficult, and her prognosis remains uncertain. However, with two dedicated institutions working flawlessly together and familiar faces by her side, every conceivable effort is being made to give Maya the best possible chance.
Article Summary: Maya, an 18-month-old critically ill orphaned elephant calf, has been airlifted from Kerala’s Abhayaranyam to Anant Ambani's Vantara in Jamnagar. The calf, who has been unable to stand following a severe fall in July, was shifted to the facility after medical experts sought advanced veterinary intervention to prevent euthanasia.

NEW DELHI: A Delhi court has allowed a complainant to submit additional documents in a case alleging that Congress MP Sonia Gandhi was included in poll rolls before acquiring Indian citizenship.The ACJM court has scheduled the next hearing for Nov 18 after the complainant's counsel sought more time to place further evidence on record.The complaint by advocate Vikas Tripathi alleges that Italian-origin Sonia's name appeared on the voter list of New Delhi parliamentary constituency in 1980, before she acquired Indian citizenship on April 30, 1983. Her name was allegedly deleted in 1982 and reinstated in 1983, also before she became an Indian citizen.A sessions court had in Sept this year set aside an order by the ACJM refusing to order an FIR against Sonia. Judge Vishal Gogne allowed the appeal by Tripathi saying the ACJM's rejection was based on an unverified photocopy of a record and constituted a "non-speaking (unreasoned)" order.Gogne emphasised that electoral rolls were meant exclusively for citizens and rejected the ACJM court's observations on the roles of the Centre and Election Commission as "improper".

Article Title: How Abdullahs managed the rebellion: Farooq calls MLAs’ demands genuine, Omar offers to resign
Article Text:
Omar Abdullah and Farooq Abdullah

SRINAGAR: With National Conference (NC) facing its biggest internal challenge in recent decades, party president Farooq Abdullah and Jammu & Kashmir chief minister Omar Abdullah held a meeting with 15 of the 25 rebel MLAs at the former’s residence for over two hours on Friday morning in a bid to defuse the crisis.While Farooq sought to mollify the rebels by terming their demands “genuine”, Omar sought to play the emotional card by offering to resign several times during the meeting, construing the criticism of his cabinet ministers and his adviser Nasir Aslam Wani as akin to questioning his leadership. He walked out of the meeting at least three times before being persuaded by the MLAs to return, sources said.While the rebels’ key demands — replacing all eight ministers, including deputy CM Surinder Choudhary, and removing Wani — remained unresolved, the meeting agreed on setting up consultative committees of legislators for each cabinet minister and a separate manifesto committee to monitor the implementation of the party’s election promises, including the restoration of J&K’s special status, sources said.This is the first time in around four decades that NC MLAs have openly challenged the party leadership, creating a crisis for the Omar govt.After the meeting, Farooq, flanked by Omar and the MLAs, addressed media persons and dismissed suggestions of a split or rebellion within NC. The party remained “united and strong”, he asserted.“We have spoken to the legislators, and their concerns and grievances are genuine.We will give due consideration to them. Everyone was heard patiently. Some (confidence-building) measures will be taken soon, while others will be implemented gradually. We will work to strengthen the party and the govt so that people’s problems are addressed,” he said.The NC chief reiterated that the party would continue its fight for the restoration of statehood and Article 370.Bashir Ahmad Shah Veeri, MLA from Bijbehara in south Kashmir, said, “We remain committed to Article 370. It took BJP almost 70 years to declare it done and dusted; our fight (for its restoration) has not even completed four years so far ... you will see in the coming days how aggressively we pursue the restoration of statehood.”Another rebel legislator told TOI that the party leadership had agreed to consider a cabinet reshuffle within a year. “The meeting went well and I think all our demands to strengthen the party were accepted,” he said.
Article Summary: National Conference (NC) facing its biggest internal challenge in recent decades. Party president Farooq Abdullah and Jammu & Kashmir chief minister Omar Abdullah held a meeting with 15 of the 25 rebel MLAs at the former’s residence for over two hours on Friday morning.

NEW DELHI: Sikkim HC, with a sanctioned strength of three judges but a working strength of two, is unable to hear intra-court appeals against judgements rendered by two single-judge benches headed by the chief justice and the other judge.Pendency of appeals against single-judge bench's orders has forced Sikkim CJ A Muhammed Mustaque to write to CJI Surya Kant for issuance of appropriate orders "for facilitating transfer of five pending writ appeals to another high court or making such other suitable arrangement in the interest of justice".A bench of CJI Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana Friday treated the Sikkim CJ's letter on the administrative side as a suo motu writ petition and sought response from the Centre.Sikkim CJ, in his letter, said, "The continued pendency of these matters, owing to the aforesaid institutional constraint, may adversely affect the timely dispensation of justice and legitimate expectations of the litigants. The situation, therefore, calls for appropriate consideration so that the appeals may be heard and adjudicated upon without undue delay."Justice Mustaque became CJ of Sikkim HC on Jan 4. In June, the HC's first woman judge Meenakshi M Rai became CJ of Patna HC, reducing Sikkim's working strength to two, the other judge in the HC being Justice Bhaskar Raj Pradhan.
Article Summary: Pendency of appeals against single-judge bench's orders forced Sikkim CJ to write to CJI Surya Kant. CJI asked for transfer of five pending writ appeals to another high court or other suitable arrangement in the interest of justice. A bench of CJI Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana Friday treated the CJ's letter as a suo motu writ petition.

Article Title: PG doctors quit premier medical institutes
Article Text:
Representative image

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Postgraduate doctors are walking away from residency programmes at some of India's leading medical institutions. RTI replies show exits across AIIMS campuses and JIPMER , with AIIMS Delhi alone reporting 34 junior resident departures in 2025.While several institutes lack consolidated data on psychiatric counselling or workplace stress among residents, Dr Lakshya Mittal, chairperson of United Doctors Front (UDF), said multiple RTI applications filed by its members had revealed postgraduate doctors quitting premier medical institutions despite securing top NEET-PG ranks. He cited complaints of duties extending beyond 36 hours, workplace harassment, toxic work culture and inadequate support.“Residency is meant to train doctors, not break them. Discipline is not humiliation and dedication is not exploitation,” Mittal said, urging authorities to enforce working-hour regulations, establish independent grievance-redressal mechanisms and fix institutional accountability. UDF has also filed a PIL in the Supreme Court.However, the figures from individual institutions show that departures have continued, even as some reported a decline.At AIIMS Delhi, 34 junior resident doctors quit in 2025, compared with 60 in 2024, a decline of about 43%. The number of residents joining also fell, from 324 in 2024 to 267 in 2025. Department-wise figures show the highest number of exits in anaesthesiology at seven, followed by ophthalmology at six. Surgery reported three exits, as did pathology. Ophthalmology had recorded 14 exits in 2024.JIPMER, Puducherry, also reported a decline in resignations. A combined count of departures from its January and July batches shows 44 residents resigned in 2025, compared with 60 in 2024, a fall of nearly 27%. However, exits continued across several specialities, including anaesthesiology, emergency medicine, orthopaedics, pathology and surgery.The trend is not confined to these two institutions. AIIMS Kalyani reported 15 exits across all three years of postgraduate training in 2025, including 13 from the January and July batches. Another 11 students from the 2026 batches had left by the time of its reply. AIIMS Raipur reported 19 exits from its 2025 batches, AIIMS Patna 12, while AIIMS Gorakhpur also reported departures. At AIIMS Rishikesh, 30 students across various postgraduate and super-speciality programmes left in 2025.The RTI also sought details of psychiatric counselling and whether stress, depression or sleep deprivation were recorded as reasons for leaving. AIIMS Delhi said it had no compiled counselling data, while AIIMS Rishikesh reported six postgraduate students receiving psychiatric counselling in 2026 but maintained no consolidated record of workplace-related stress. AIIMS Raipur reported no residents seeking counselling in 2025 or 2026.AIIMS Patna reported 15 residents receiving counselling in 2025 and none in 2026, while AIIMS Kalyani declined to provide the information, citing RTI provisions.The figures are not directly comparable as institutes provided data for different periods and batches. While they establish that residents are leaving, the reasons remain unclear, with several institutes lacking records that could help explain the departures.
Article Summary: Postgraduate doctors are walking away from residency programmes at some of India's leading medical institutions. RTI replies show exits across AIIMS campuses and JIPMER. At AIIMs Delhi, 34 junior resident doctors quit in 2025, compared with 60 in 2024, a decline of about 43%. exits continued across several specialities, including anaesthesiology.

NEW DELHI: Congress Parliamentary Party (CPP) Chairperson Sonia Gandhi has accused the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) government of causing significant damage to India's democratic institutions over the past 12 years, expressing confidence that the country's electorate would eventually bring about a return to proper governance.In an interview with The Hindu, Sonia said the damage extended to the country's democratic fabric and institutions, adding that people were increasingly recognising the consequences of the government's actions."Over the last twelve years, great damage has been done to the fabric of our country, our democracy and our institutions," she said.She expressed optimism about the country's political future, while acknowledging that restoring democratic institutions and governance would require considerable time and effort, even after the present government leaves office."Even after this government goes, it will take time to restore our systems to health, and great effort from political parties. People are now beginning to be restless and recognising the damage. But I am optimistic, and I know that the people of India will welcome a return to proper governance," she said.Reflecting on the 1975 Emergency imposed by former Prime Minister Indira Gandhi, Sonia Gandhi acknowledged that democratic rights had been curtailed during the 21-month period but said the decision was taken constitutionally."It was only after the Emergency that I came to know the true gravity of what had been happening. Yes, democratic rights had been curtailed, and there was a suspension of habeas corpus, but it was done constitutionally," she said.She also offered her perspective on the circumstances leading to the imposition of the Emergency, referring to violent protests, attacks on government offices and public transport, widespread unrest and calls for the bureaucracy and armed forces to disobey orders.Also read: Court allows more evidence in Sonia Gandhi voter list case "Yet, when I take myself back to that period and try and see it from Mrs Gandhi's (Indira Gandhi) point of view, I see her struggling to cope with the rapidly deteriorating prevailing circumstances: violent protests, government offices and public transport set on fire, widespread organised unrest and even a call for the bureaucracy and armed forces to disobey orders," she said.Sonia further noted that Indira Gandhi eventually recognised the situation, called for general elections in March 1977 and later publicly acknowledged and apologised for the excesses committed during the Emergency."Hindsight allows us to put things better in perspective. Let's not forget that it was Mrs Gandhi herself who came to recognise what was happening and called for the March 1977 election. And you know very well that she herself later publicly expressed regret and apologised for excesses during the Emergency," she said.Rahul Gandhi reacted to Sonia's interview, saying in a post on X, "Sixty years in public life, and still the same person. Proud of you, Ma."Meanwhile, the BJP hit back at Sonia Gandhi over her criticism of the central government, with Union Law Minister Arjun Ram Meghwal invoking the 1975 Emergency and questioning her remarks on democracy.Speaking to reporters in Bikaner, Rajasthan, Meghwal said Gandhi should also recall the period when democratic rights were curtailed, opposition leaders were jailed and journalists were silenced."The article makes certain observations regarding democracy. I would like to ask Sonia ji: does she not recall the period of 1975, when democracy was strangled? Thousands of senior leaders from various political parties were thrown into jail, and the voices of journalists were silenced. She ought to remember that era as well. In contrast, over the last 12 years, PM Modi has nurtured, flourished, and strengthened democracy, proclaiming to the entire world that India is the 'mother of democracy. ' It is Prime Minister Narendra Modi who has emphatically declared that 'India is the mother of democracy,'" he said.Responding to the opposition's demand for a special parliamentary session, Meghwal said the government was ready for a debate and urged opposition parties to submit a proposal. He also referred to the Home Minister's remarks at a rally in Haryana, saying Parliament was the appropriate forum for such discussions."Our Home Minister provided a fitting response (to Rahul Gandhi) at a rally in Haryana, pointing out that the Constitution-makers designated Parliament as the proper venue for such debates. If the opposition wishes to engage in a discussion, let them put forward a proposal; we can certainly convene a special session—there is no issue with that. The Prime Minister has also expressed a similar sentiment. As for the suggestion that someone should act as a 'judge'—our democratic system already has a mechanism for this; the Speaker serves as the arbiter. What is new about this proposal? Why not simply debate? Who is stopping them? They have written requesting a special session; the government is prepared to call one. We are ready for a debate," he said.Reacting to Sonia’s article, Union Minister Giriraj Singh launched a sharp attack on her, questioning her remarks on democracy and making allegations about her and her son’s citizenship."Sonia Gandhi, may God grant you a long life. You lived in this country for 12 years without citizenship, and it is alleged that you even cast a vote. Questions are also being raised regarding your son's citizenship. Abandon these ambitions. Forget about a return in 10 years; the Congress will never return to power in this country. You haven't held power in nine different states for the last 40 years. Sonia Gandhi, from the very Congress party that imposed the Emergency and silenced the voices of the people, is talking about democracy. You and your son are trying to incite a civil war in India; that ambition, too, will never be fulfilled."The Congress leader also spoke about her upcoming memoir, Belonging: A Journey of Love, describing it as an account of how she grew to love her husband and former Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi's family and India, and how that connection eventually brought her into public life.In the interview, she said she had long been reluctant to share her personal story but eventually decided to write about the experiences that shaped her life and her decision to enter politics."I had no desire to talk about it for so long. But it is not only a love story between the two of us, but it's also the story of how I grew to love Rajiv's family and the country to which they belonged, and then I too came to belong in it. And of how this love brought me into public life, when I saw the purpose of all the sacrifices they had made being threatened, and the party was weakening. I felt I had to do something," she said.The memoir traces Sonia's journey from her childhood in post-war Italy and her romance with Rajiv Gandhi, which brought her to India, to the personal losses that shaped her life and her relationship with her adopted country. It also recounts her experiences as a member of the Nehru-Gandhi family and her journey from private life to public service.The book, her first memoir, is scheduled to be launched on November 10.Earlier, Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi had expressed his excitement over the publication of his mother's memoir, saying he was proud that her personal story would reach readers.On the 82nd birth anniversary of his father, Rajiv Gandhi, Rahul said he understood how difficult it had been for his mother, who preferred to maintain a private life, to share her experiences publicly."I am happy, and so proud, that your story--'Belonging: A Journey of Love'--will finally be read by the millions of people who love you. I know how hard it was for someone as private as you to tell the world your beautiful story. Today, on his birthday, I can see Papa smiling and looking down proudly at his beautiful Sonia," Rahul Gandhi said.

NEW DELHI: Two men have been arrested and charged in connection with the shooting at comedian Kapil Sharma's restaurant in Surrey, Canada, last year, police said.The incident took place on October 16, 2025, when shots were fired at the restaurant for the third time since it opened in July that year.The Royal Canadian Mounted Police (RCMP) said in a statement on Friday that the two suspects, Pardeep Singh and Saveer Khan, both aged 22, were arrested on November 1. Article Title: Kindness, the best revenge
Article Text:
A Letter to a Hindoo’

“Inna Seithaarai OruththalAavarNaana

Nannayam seithu vidal”

vidal

We live in an age when historical incidents are quoted with absolute confidence, often without checking their origins. A good story, it appears, needs neither evidence nor a source. The more dramatic it sounds, the faster it travels.Consider the famous epitaph attributed to Alexander the Great: “A tomb now suffices him for whom the world was not enough.” Beautiful as it sounds, this was a later literary reflection, not an authenticated inscription on Alexander's tomb.It is said that the French Revolution was triggered when Queen Marie Antoinette, ignorant of the sufferings of people, said “Let them eat cake” if they do not have bread. The infamous quotation was never uttered by her; French writer Rousseau had written a similar phrase in 1766, when Marie was only ten years old.Napoleon is frequently described as a short man, often invoked to demonstrate that courage has nothing to do with one’s height. In reality, he was approximately 5'7", slightly above the average French male of his time. Julius Caesar was not born through a Caesarean section; his mother survived well into his adulthood. Shah Jahan never ordered that the hands of thousands of Taj Mahal workers be amputated. Nor did an apple famously fall on Newton's head and trigger his discovery of gravity.These stories have acquired lives of their own, often at the expense of history.One such story closer to home involves Mahatma Gandhi , Leo Tolstoy and the Thirukkural .Gandhi is said to have learnt about the Thirukkural from Tolstoy and subsequently adopted ahimsa as an instrument of India's freedom struggle. It makes for a wonderful story, but the documented sequence is different.Gandhi had heard already about the Thirukkural from the Tamil community of South Africa and had come across G U Pope’s translation. And his philosophy of non-violence originated from his upbringing. Tolstoy merely referred to a particular couplet of Valluvar that deeply resonated with Gandhi's existing convictions.In 1908, an Indian revolutionary, Taraknath Das, wrote to Tolstoy seeking support for India's independence. Tolstoy responded with an open letter titled ‘– a 6,000 worded document. In one section, Tolstoy quoted five couplets from what he called the 'Hindu Kural'. Having come across the Thirukkural through a German translation, he was deeply moved by Valluvar's philosophy of compassion, particularly the principle of returning good for evil.In 1909, Gandhi came across Tolstoy's letter. He wrote to him to verify its authenticity and to seek permission to translate and publish it in an Indian language. Tolstoy readily agreed. Gandhi published this in his journal, Indian Opinion.One of the couplets quoted by Tolstoy and particularly appealed to Gandhi was Kural 314:“Punish an evil doer by shaming him with aGood deed and forget both”The subtlety lies in the final word,— to let go, to forget. One must not merely return good for evil; one must also relinquish the memory of the injury.Perhaps that is the most beautiful part of this history. Three remarkable minds, separated by geography and language, connected by one timeless thought.History needs no embellishment to be fascinating. We need not manufacture conversations or invent letters to make our heritage relevant. Truth has its own poetry. We only need the patience to discover it before falsehood travels halfway around the world.
Article Summary: In 1908, an Indian revolutionary, Taraknath Das, wrote to Tolstoy seeking support for India's independence. In one section of the open letter titled ‘– a 6,000 worded document. – TolStoy quoted five couplets from what he called the ‘Hindu Kural’ One of the couplets, Kural 314, particularly appealed to Gandhi and he adopted ahimsa as an instrument of India's freedom struggle.

NEW DELHI: Acknowledging that the enormous amount of judicial time spent over the years to tackle pollution in Delhi had yielded only marginal benefits, Supreme Court Friday said when more and more restrictions, without scientific basis, were put in place, people tended to violate them with a vengeance, reports Dhananjay Mahapatra.Reflecting on numerous orders and subsequent monitoring of their implementation to improve air quality, a bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana said, "To think we can achieve air quality of less than 100 (AQI) in Delhi during winters is utopian when 'very poor' and 'severe' have become the new normal."When amicus curiae and senior advocate Aparajita Singh flagged news reports on normal crackers being sold as green crackers and attributed part of the rising pollution to it, the ben-ch said the capital was witnessing bumper-to-bumper traf-fic for the last few days and wi-th so many cars remaining on the road for so many extra hours, it must be adding to the pollution load.Additional solicitor general Aishwarya Bhati attributed the traffic congestion to the festive season and senior advocate Sanjiv Sen, who was appearing for MCD, said the culture of distribution of gifts was one of the major reasons for the huge spurt in road traffic.At this juncture, Singh drew the court's attention to sale of normal crackers as green crackers in flagrant violation of court orders and warned of a huge post-Diwali spike in pollution levels.The bench said, "Diwali celebrations must be accompanied with public awareness campaigns. It is awareness that alone can curb pollution. No number of restrictions is going to work. More the number of orders from the court, the more the violations. That is the tendency of people. We will go by expert advice."The CJI said local councillors must create awareness among people. The bench said it would pass some orders and seek compliance from NCR states.Bhati informed the court that the Commission on Air Quality Management (CAQM), the expert body tasked with devising and implementing short-term, intermediate and long-term measures to tackle air pollution, had put Grad-ed Response Action Plan (GRAP) in place."Each stage of GRAP triggers more restrictions - stoppage of construction, bar on entry of BS-IV emission standard vehicles, sprinkling of water, staggered office hours," she said, adding that there was a massive augmentation of clean fuel public transport. "But every human activity contributes to pollution," Bhati added, pointing out that factories in Delhi operated on clean fuel and thermal power plants had been closed.She said the main polluti-on load came from vehicles as Delhi had a staggering numb-er of them. "Major contribu-tor to pollution in Delhi is vehicles and other local sources. Stubble burning in winters, which has drastically declined in Haryana and to some extent in Punjab, tips the scales because of the unique geographical position of Delhi and the wind direction make the national capital a receptor of pollution," the ASG said.Singh said monitoring implementation of anti-pollution measures was crucial and complained that transport vehicles continued to idle at MCD toll plazas at 126 entry points. Refuting the claim, Sen said after the integration of technology, no transport vehicle idled at any of the nine toll plazas, which handle 90% of commercial traffic into Delhi.
Article Summary: Supreme Court said when more and more restrictions, without scientific basis, were put in place, people tended to violate them. Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana said, "To think we can achieve air quality of less than 100 (AQI) in Delhi during winters is utopian when'very poor' and'severe' have become the new normal"

In this Diwali edition of the Knowledge Series, Sanjiv Kaura, CEO-CSR, The Times of India, speaks with iImpact catalyst Aruna Lohia Goenka about abundance, one of the five pillars of her YASHA philosophy. From the paradox of wealthy people who feel poor to the extraordinary power of love, gratitude and consciousness, the conversation explores why prosperity begins not with what we possess, but with how we experience life.Diwali is a celebration of prosperity. But you seem to believe that abundance has very little to do with how much money we have.!(Laughs) Oh, Sanjiv! Money is wonderful. I have nothing against it.! But abundance is not a number in your bank account. Abundance is a feeling. And at its heart, it is a feeling of love. You can have very little and feel wonderfully abundant. Equally, you can possess extraordinary wealth and still feel desperately poor. Because poverty, too, can be a feeling.So, theoretically, I could be a billionaire and still be poor?(Smiles) Not theoretically, Sanjiv. Quite possibly! You can rule the world and still lack consciousness. You can have power over millions of people and yet have no mastery over your own mind. What good is owning the world if you wake up every morning feeling that something is missing? The opposite of abundance is not necessarily poverty. Sometimes, it is the inability to recognise what we already have.Take the example of Rajat Gupta, the former global head of McKinsey. Despite extraordinary professional success, he has spoken about feeling relatively poor when comparing himself with people whose wealth was vastly greater. Imagine that! A man who had reached the pinnacle of professional achievement could still experience a sense of not having enough!But isn't that rather difficult when the world constantly reminds us that somebody else has more?You have identified one of the greatest enemies of abundance: comparison. We look at someone else's house, car, career, success or lifestyle, and suddenly what made us happy yesterday seems inadequate today.! (Laughs) Isn't that extraordinary? Nothing has actually been taken away from us. Yet we have somehow managed to make ourselves feel poorer.! Comparison can turn abundance into scarcity without changing a single thing in our lives.You often speak about consciousness. But how does one actually develop an abundant consciousness?Begin by recognising what already exists in your life. Your health. Your relationships. The ability to learn. The opportunity to serve. The sunrise you did not have to purchase. The love you did not have to earn through a financial transaction. (Laughs) Imagine if the uUniverse started sending us invoices for sunlight, fresh air and the affection of our loved ones! We might suddenly discover that we are much wealthier than we thought. But gratitude is only the beginning. Abundant consciousness also means recognising possibilities where others see limitations, and opportunities to contribute where others see only competition.You mentioned love. Why is love so central to your understanding of abundance?Because love changes our relationship with the world. When we operate from scarcity, we ask, "What can I get?" When we operate from abundance, we begin asking, "What can I give?" Love, compassion, kindness and encouragement are extraordinary forms of wealth. And unlike many material possessions, sharing them does not diminish what we have. A candle loses nothing by lighting another candle. And on Diwali, isn't that a particularly beautiful thought?But surely we cannot tell someone struggling to feed their family that poverty is merely a feeling?Absolutely not! That would be both insensitive and wrong. Material deprivation is real. Hunger is real. Lack of healthcare, education and opportunity is real. We have a collective responsibility to address them. When I say poverty can also be a feeling, I am speaking about the inner experience of scarcity, not denying economic hardship. In fact, an abundant consciousness should make us more conscious of other people's suffering, not less. True abundance is not indifference to poverty. It is the determination to ensure that others can also flourish.Is there a danger that gratitude might make people complacent? If I feel I have enough, why strive for more?(Laughs) Sanjiv, gratitude is not retirement from ambition.! Be grateful for what you have while remaining excited about what you can create. The difference is whether your ambition comes from fear or possibility. Scarcity says, "I must achieve more because I am not enough." Abundance says, "I am grateful for who I am, and excited about what I can become." Contentment and ambition are not enemies. One gives us peace; the other gives us purpose.How does this philosophy of abundance connect with your YASHA vision for Viksit Bharat 2047?YASHA brings together Yuva, Anna, Shiksha, Hunar and Abundance. To me, aAbundance is also the spirit that connects the other four. What is the purpose of educating our children if they grow up believing that success means defeating somebody else? What is the purpose of developing skills if we do not use them to create opportunities for others? What is the purpose of prosperity if it does not lead to shared wellbeing?Imagine 1.4 billion people with an abundant consciousness. People who recognise their own possibilities, celebrate the success of others and contribute whatever they can to the nation. A Bharat where we do not measure our happiness by how much more our neighbour possesses, but by how much better we can make life for one another.One final Diwali message?This Diwali, light a lamp in your home. But also light one within your consciousness. Let it illuminate gratitude where there was comparison, love where there was fear,and possibility where there was scarcity. Don't wait to become wealthy to feel abundant. Feel abundant, and use that consciousness to create wealth - for yourself, for others and for Bharat.Because when 1.4 billion people begin to think, feel and act with abundance, Viksit Bharat 2047 will be much more than an economic achievement. It will be a flourishing of human consciousness. And that, Sanjiv, is what I call the magic of the Universe.
Article Summary: iImpact catalyst Aruna Lohia Goenka talks with Sanjiv Kaura, CEO-CSR, The Times of India. The conversation explores why prosperity begins not with what we possess, but with how we experience life. Love, compassion and kindness are extraordinary forms of wealth.

NEW DELHI: The Election Commission (EC) on Friday announced that voters excluded from the draft electoral rolls during the ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise in seven states will be given another opportunity to have their names included in the final electoral rolls.The directive applies to electors who were issued enumeration forms but were left out of the draft rolls after being categorised as Absent, Shifted, Dead or Duplicate (ASDD). The seven states covered are Delhi, Maharashtra, Haryana, Andhra Pradesh, Jharkhand, Telangana and Nagaland.The EC has also directed officials to put in place a monitoring mechanism to ensure that no eligible voter is denied the opportunity to be included in the final electoral rolls, while simultaneously preventing duplicate enrolments."In cases where such an elector who was marked as ASDD and consequently whose name does not appear in the draft electoral roll, has shifted the place of residence within the state, such elector is not required to submit Form-8, instead he/she shall submit enumeration form along with the statement enclosed herewith as Annexure-C (indicating the new address and the assembly constituency)," the EC said in a statement.The poll body also clarified that electors who have already submitted Form-6 for fresh enrolment during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise need not submit the enumeration form and accompanying statement again. Their applications will be processed in accordance with the Commission's clarification dated November 3."Partially filled enumeration forms in respect of all such ASDD electors would be generated afresh in ERO dashboard in ECINET. The DEOs/EROs shall make all possible efforts to contact such electors through the concerned Booth Level Officers (BLOs) and ensure delivery of the enumeration forms either physically or through electronic means such as WhatsApp, e-mail or SMS, wherever contact details are available," the Commission stated.The EC further directed BLOs to coordinate with Booth Level Agents (BLAs) of various political parties to reach out to the affected electors. This would include house-to-house visits, enquiries with neighbours, family members and Resident Welfare Associations (RWAs), as well as contacting voters through available phone numbers wherever feasible.
Article Summary: The directive applies to electors who were issued enumeration forms but were left out of the draft rolls after being categorised as Absent, Shifted, Dead or Duplicate. The seven states covered are Delhi, Maharashtra, Haryana, Andhra Pradesh, Jharkhand, Telangana and Nagaland.

US President Donald Trump on Monday confused India with Brazil, claiming that 125 million people had voted in an Indian “presidential election”, while also questioning the integrity of the American voting system.In a post on Truth Social, Trump wrote, “125 Million People voted today in the first round of India’s Presidential Election. The results came out shortly after the vote closed, on the same day!”He then compared the alleged election results with the US electoral process, writing, “In Detroit, Philadelphia, California, and numerous other US Cities and States, the results, with much smaller numbers, will often take weeks to Rig, I mean, calculate. Voting in America is corrupt!!!”However, India did not hold a presidential election on Sunday. The President of India is elected indirectly by an electoral college and not through a direct nationwide popular vote.Trump's remarks came after Brazil held the first round of its presidential election on Sunday, with incumbent President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and right-wing challenger Flávio Bolsonaro advancing to the October 25 runoff.With 99.99% of the votes counted, Bolsonaro secured 47.03% of the valid votes, while Lula received 45.16%, according to Brazil's Superior Electoral Court.The figure of around 125 million mentioned by Trump is close to Brazil's total valid votes, which stood at about 125.27 million, suggesting he may have confused the Brazilian election with India.Neither Bolsonaro nor Lula crossed the 50% threshold required to win in the first round, triggering the October 25 runoff, BBC reported.Flávio Bolsonaro, the son of former Brazilian president Jair Bolsonaro, outperformed expectations in the first round and finished ahead of Lula. His strong showing has raised the prospect of a shift to the right in Latin America's largest economy.Brazil has used electronic voting for decades, and electoral authorities said the first-round voting process proceeded smoothly.The Organization of American States' electoral observation mission said “the voting has been going smoothly and under adequate safety conditions.”The rapid announcement of results has also been cited as a strength of Brazil's electronic voting system.“When results take a lot of time, it creates an opening for people to cast doubt on the results, to say there’s been a problem,” Josemar Lauriano Pereira, a 46-year-old lawyer in Rio de Janeiro, told the Associated Press.Trump's post drew reactions on social media, with users pointing out that India does not elect its president through a direct popular vote.One user posted, “Trump living in a different world? Is a presidential election taking place in India? President Donald Trump made the incorrect claim that 125 million people voted in India's "presidential election" today.”Another said, “What is my blud Donald Trump smoking? Why is he mentioning India instead of Brazil when talking about the election?”

Article Title: In 2021, Josh Allen bought land in Orchard Park; his New York mansion and California farm show his life beyond the NFL

Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen has a life that connects two very different places, California and New York. While he spends most of the NFL season in Buffalo, his story began on a family farm in Firebaugh, California. From working in cotton fields as a child to owning a $7.2 million house in Dana Point, Allen’s journey offers an interesting look at his life away from football.Josh Allen was born on May 21, 1996, in Firebaugh, California, a small farming town in the state’s Central Valley, around 40 miles west of Fresno. He grew up there with his parents, Joel and Lavonne Allen, and his three siblings. Long before he became the face of the Buffalo Bills, his everyday life involved helping his family with agricultural work.Farming was not a new business for the Allens. His father, Joel, comes from a long line of farmers, and the family has been connected to the agricultural community for generations. According to a 2021 report by the Los Angeles Times, the extended Allen family owned around 1,200 acres of farmland in the Firebaugh area.The land has played an important role in shaping Josh’s childhood. During summer breaks, he often worked alongside his younger brother instead of spending all his time playing sports.His responsibilities included pulling weeds, digging ditches, moving irrigation pipes and helping with cotton fields.The Los Angeles Times reported that Allen also drove tractors while working on the farm. These were not occasional visits to a family property. He was expected to help with the regular work, just like other members of the family.His childhood in Firebaugh also gave him a close connection to the local community. His father once described the town to the Los Angeles Times by saying, “Our community, it’s a pretty special place. We kind of take care of each other.”That connection has remained important even after Allen moved away to build his football career.The Allen family has continued its farming business even as Josh’s NFL career has grown. Cantaloupes have been one of its main products, with the family also working on expanding its agricultural operation through pistachio farming.In an August 2025 report by The Westside Express, Joel Allen explained that the family had started Allen Family Orchards in 2021. At the time, the operation covered around 600 acres, with plans to add more land and eventually reach 1,000 acres.Pistachios have also become an important part of the family’s plans. The 2025 report explained that the family expected 2026 to be its first major production year for the crop. Josh has also been involved in promoting pistachios through a partnership with Wonderful Pistachios.However, the family’s farming connection is no longer limited to California. In September 2026, Joel and Lavonne brought their agricultural business to Western New York through a partnership with Tops Friendly Markets.According to WGRZ, the JA17 Allen Family Farms cantaloupes returned to participating Tops stores, giving Buffalo residents an opportunity to buy products grown by the quarterback’s family. The family also introduced merchandise, including T-shirts, hats, mugs and tote bags.There was a community reason behind the project as well. A portion of the proceeds from the melon sales and merchandise was set to support the Patricia Allen Fund at Golisano Children’s Hospital of Buffalo.Joel explained that the family wanted to use the partnership to support a community that had welcomed their son. His mother, Lavonne, also described Buffalo as a second home for the family.For Allen, this connection brings together the two places that have played major roles in his life. His family continues to work in California, while their products have found a place among Bills supporters in New York.California may be where Josh Allen grew up, but Buffalo has become his professional home. The quarterback joined the Bills in 2018 after being selected seventh overall in the NFL Draft. Since then, he has made the Buffalo area an important part of his life.Allen owns property in Orchard Park, a suburb of Buffalo where the Bills’ stadium and training facilities are located. According to Realtor.com, he purchased land in the area in 2021 for around $500,000 and later had a custom-built mansion developed there.The property sits on approximately 31 acres, giving Allen plenty of private space away from the attention that comes with being an NFL star. Its location is also convenient for his football commitments, as it is around eight minutes from Highmark Stadium.The Orchard Park estate has several features that make it stand out. Reports describe a large swimming pool, a separate pool house and a private sports court that can be used for basketball and tennis. The property also has a private par-3 golf hole, giving Allen another way to enjoy his time away from football.His connection to Orchard Park goes beyond owning an expensive property. Living close to the Bills’ facilities allows him to remain connected to the team throughout the season without having to travel far for practices and other commitments.According to Mansion Global, Allen also owns two homes in Orchard Park. However, detailed information about the interiors and current arrangements of his private residences has not been publicly confirmed.Unlike his California property, which has been listed for sale, there has been no comparable confirmed announcement that he is selling his Orchard Park estate.Apart from his property in New York, Josh Allen also has a connection to Southern California through his Dana Point house. He purchased the property in 2023 for $7.2 million, according to Mansion Global. The house is located in Monarch Bay, a gated coastal community in Orange County.The property covers approximately 2,808 square feet and has four bedrooms and three bathrooms. Built in 1962, it features a single-level design with mid-century architecture. The house also has large windows and sliding glass doors that connect the indoor living areas to the backyard.The main living space includes a family room with high ceilings, a formal dining area and a kitchen with quartz countertops. The primary bedroom has a separate sitting area, while the backyard offers outdoor space, a hot tub and patio areas.Another attraction is the location. The property is around half a mile from the beach, and residents of Monarch Bay have access to the private Monarch Bay Beach Club.Allen’s plans for the house changed after his purchase. In July 2025, he reportedly put the property on the market for $8.5 million. However, it was taken off the market in January 2026.The quarterback made another attempt to sell it in September 2026, this time with a reduced asking price of $7.95 million. Realtor.com reported the new listing on September 14, while Mansion Global also covered his second attempt to sell the property.The decision to list the Dana Point house does not mean Allen has lost his connection to California. He was born and raised in the state, and his parents and family farming business remain based there.His property choices reflect the different parts of his life. Orchard Park keeps him close to his NFL career, while Dana Point offered a place to enjoy California’s warmer weather during the offseason. Firebaugh, meanwhile, remains the place where his family’s story began.
Article Summary: Josh Allen was born on May 21, 1996, in Firebaugh, California, a small farming town in the state’s Central Valley. His father, Joel, comes from a long line of farmers, and the family has been connected to the agricultural community for generations. The extended Allen family owned around 1,200 acres of farmland in the Firebaugh area. In 2021, Josh Allen bought land in Orchard Park, a suburb of Buffalo, for around $500,000. He later had a custom-built mansion built on approximately 31,000 acres.

Pollution monitori-ng agencies are expecting the pollution levels to become severe by Saturday.According to IITM’s forecast, the share of pollution from stubble burning in neighbouring states has started to spike over the past week and has since been fluctuating around 13% to 20%, with decision support system’s models expecting the share to drop.“The outlook for the subsequent 6 days: air quality is likely to be in the severe to very poor category,” stated the air quality early warning system by IITM.

Article Title: ‘Some legends don't say goodbye’: Ex-India cricketer's heartfelt message for Mohammed Shami after Test retirement
Article Text:
Mohammad Shami (AFP Photo)

A 12-year journey in India's Test colours

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Former India cricketer and ex-Bengal captain Manoj Tiwary paid an emotional tribute to Mohammed Shami after the veteran fast bowler announced his retirement from Test cricket on Friday, bringing the curtain down on a 12-year career in the longest format.Tiwary, who had the opportunity to lead Bengal with Shami in his bowling attack, took to X to reflect on the pacer's impact and recall his association with the speedster. He described Shami as a warrior, while also highlighting the lasting memories he had created through his performances in the red-ball format."The red ball may no longer be in his hands, but the memories of his thunderbolts will forever remain in the hearts of cricket lovers. Some legends don't say goodbye; they simply become history," Tiwary wrote.Recalling his time as Bengal captain, he added: "This what it meant to me When I was leading the bengal team and having Shami in the bowling line up. Warrior at heart"Shami's announcement brings an end to an impressive Test career spanning 64 matches, during which he picked up 229 wickets. The 36-year-old made the announcement through an Instagram post, confirming that while he would no longer represent India in the white jersey, he intended to continue playing white-ball cricket."I am leaving the white jersey, but never the memories connected to it. When I first wore India's Test jersey, I had only a dream — to do something for my country. After that every wicket, every struggle, every injury and every comeback taught me something," Shami wrote."Test cricket is not just a format for me, it is a very special part of my life. Today I am deciding to retire from Test cricket with a heavy heart and unlimited beautiful memories," he added.Shami made his Test debut against the West Indies at Kolkata's Eden Gardens on November 6, 2013. He ended his career with 229 wickets at an average of 27.71, including six five-wicket hauls.His ability to extract movement through seam and swing with both the new and old ball made him a crucial member of India's pace attack across different conditions.Of his 229 wickets, 131 came in 35 Tests played in South Africa, the West Indies and India, where he maintained an average of under 25.South Africa witnessed some of Shami's finest performances in Test cricket. During India's 2018 tour, he produced a match-winning spell of 5/28 in the second innings of the Johannesburg Test, helping the visitors secure a consolation victory.On India's subsequent visit to the country, he continued his impressive record by claiming eight wickets in the series-opening Test at Centurion.Shami's final appearance in Test cricket came in the 2023 World Test Championship final against Australia at Lord's. Injuries later disrupted his career, and he remained out of the Indian team after the 2025 Champions Trophy, before deciding to bring his red-ball journey to a close.
Article Summary: Mohammad Shami retires from Test cricket after 12-year career. Former Bengal captain Manoj Tiwary pays tribute to fast bowler. Shami made his Test debut against the West Indies at Kolkata's Eden Gardens in 2013. He ended his career with 229 wickets at an average of 27.71.

Article Title: LeBron James’ son Bronny James faces major roster decision amid struggle in Los Angeles Lakers
Article Text:
Bronny James. Image via: Katelyn Mulcahy/ Getty Images

Why did the Lakers send Bronny James to the G League?

What does Bronny James’ contract say about his future?

The Los Angeles Lakers assigned Bronny James to the Coachella Valley Lakers on Thursday, and nobody has said when he will be back. The 22-year-old guard has played 12 minutes this season and has four points for a 7-2 team. The elder James left for the Philadelphia 76ers in July, making this the first season in Los Angeles without him. The younger James is signed to a fully guaranteed deal through 2026-27, with a team option for the year after. Coachella Valley opens its season Friday.Bronny James shot 25% from the floor in the preseason, going 4 of 16, and made one of eight three-pointers. Coach JJ Redick had already cast doubt on his place, saying last month, “I don’t think he’s played well in the four preseason games.”Redick had liked his September and summer work. Then the games started.The Lakers tried the 6-foot-2 guard at backup point guard while Collin Sexton was out with a calf injury. It did not work. James struggled to handle the ball, make plays and run the offense, the core jobs at that spot. And Redick went another direction. Los Angeles had 16 players on guaranteed contracts, and in October it waived Dalton Knecht, the No.17 pick in 2024, instead of James, the 55th pick in the same draft.James is guaranteed his salary through the 2026-27 season. A $2.4 million team option covers 2027-28, so the Lakers can decline it if he is not ready for NBA minutes. They took him out of USC in the second round in 2024. Matisse Thybulle and Ziaire Williams signed minimum deals this summer and are already playing 3-and-D roles, which leaves little room on the depth chart.The Lakers are building around Luka Doncic and a title run.James has produced in the G League before. ESPN’s Dave McMenamin reported he averaged 18.4 points on 49.6% shooting, with 4.4 assists and 4.0 rebounds, over 25 games for South Bay in the past two seasons. He also hit 37.9% of 158 threes last year across NBA and G League play. Those numbers point to a shooter’s role more than a playmaker’s.Rookie Cameron Carr was assigned too. The team, rebranded and moved from South Bay, plays at Acrisure Arena in Palm Desert

Article Title: Luka Doncic and LeBron James unite for major legal fight as an unexpected partnership emerges off the court
Article Text:
Luka Doncic and LeBron James. Image via: Getty Images

What did LeBron James and Luka Doncic demand from Bron AI?

Luka Doncic and LeBron James. Image via: Harry How/Getty Images

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

What have James and Doncic’s teams said about the ad?

LeBron James and Luka Doncic have each sent a cease-and-desist letter to the company behind Bron AI, a betting app that used their names and images in a social media ad this week. Spokespeople for both stars said their legal teams sent the orders. Both want their likenesses removed.The video, posted on X, showed a player in a No. 23 jersey with “Bron” on the back placing wagers on NBA players. Doncic’s name and image appeared on the phone screen. By Thursday afternoon, the post had been taken down.The demand is simple. Both stars want their names and likenesses out of the app’s marketing. The letters went to PlayVision Inc., the sports technology startup that owns Bron AI. James moved first, with his legal team calling for the ad to be removed. The Lakers star’s attorneys followed hours later with their own warning.The video leaned on James in several ways. Besides the jersey, it used an AI-generated voice that sounded like the 76ers star. Giannis Antetokounmpo, Donovan Mitchell and Dillon Brooks also appeared in the ad.The posts pulled in more than 900,000 views in under 24 hours. X removed them after Front Office Sports first reported the cease-and-desist.James left the Lakers for the 76ers in free agency this summer, so the two are no longer teammates. Doncic’s side still matched the move within hours. On the court, Doncic is averaging 38.5 points and the Lakers are 7-2, while James’ 76ers hold the league’s best record at 8-1.Adam Mendelsohn, James’ spokesperson, called the ad another sign of weak originality in sports marketing. He said the goal was probably to draw a cease-and-desist and turn the video into a story. A response is not optional in a case like this, he added, and it will not be the last of its kind. Mendelsohn said “these gimmicks never work because people see through it.”Lara Beth Seager, Doncic’s business manager, spoke more about the wider trend. She said cases like this are rising as AI tools get easier to use, calling it “something we’re dealing with more and more.” In her statement to The Athletic, she said her team will act each time Doncic’s name or likeness is used without permission.
Article Summary: LeBron James and Luka Doncic have each sent a cease-and-desist letter to the company behind Bron AI. Both stars want their names and likenesses out of the app’s marketing. The video, posted on X, showed a player in a No. 23 jersey with “Bron” on the back placing wagers on NBA players.

Article Title: In 1983, an Air Canada Boeing 767 ran out of fuel at 41,000 feet because fuel was calculated in pounds instead of kilograms; the pilots glided it onto a disused air base runway in Gimli, and all 69 on
Article Text:
Confusion over kilograms and pounds

Total power loss in mid-air

Race track diversion at Gimli

Landing on the dragstrip

An Air Canada Boeing 767 carrying 61 passengers and eight crew members ran completely out of fuel at 41,000 feet over Manitoba after a mistake in converting metric measurements caused ground staff to put less than half the required fuel into the aircraft. The pilots managed to glide the 132-tonne plane for 17 minutes without engine power. They made an emergency landing on a former military runway that had been turned into a sports car race track. According to the official inquiry by the Aviation Safety Board of Canada, all 69 people on board survived the incident on 23 July 1983. Only minor injuries were reported during the evacuation.The fueling mistake happened on the ground in Montreal before the flight departed for Edmonton via Ottawa. The aircraft's digital Fuel Quantity Indicator System (FQIS) was not working because of a faulty channel. Maintenance workers had already recorded the problem. Since the automatic fuel gauge showed no readings, the ground crew and pilots had to work out the fuel amount manually. They used a dripstick, a tool that measured the volume of fuel in litres. At the time, Air Canada was changing its fleet over to the metric system.The newly purchased Boeing 767 was the airline's first aircraft that used metric measurements throughout. The standard flight management computers required fuel amounts to be entered in kilograms. However, while doing the manual calculations, the crew used the conversion figure for pounds instead of kilograms. Instead of multiplying the fuel volume in litres by 0.8 to calculate its weight in kilograms, they multiplied it by 1.77. This was the conversion figure used for imperial measurements. Because of this mistake, the aircraft took off with just 22,300 pounds (10,100 kg) of fuel. This was only about 45 percent of the 49,200 pounds (22,300 kg) needed to complete the journey to Edmonton.While flying over Red Lake, Ontario, at 41,000 feet, the pilots received warnings about low fuel pressure in the cockpit. Captain Robert Pearson and First Officer Maurice Quintal first thought there was a problem with a fuel pump. They planned to divert the aircraft to Winnipeg. Within minutes, both Pratt & Whitney JT9D engines stopped working, cutting off power to all the main electrical generators. With both engines out, the cockpit displays went blank. The pilots were left with only a few emergency instruments powered by batteries. These backup instruments did not include a vertical speed indicator, which made it difficult for the crew to work out how quickly the aircraft was losing height. There was another serious problem. Without engine power to run the hydraulic pumps, the aircraft's control surfaces could no longer be moved using the normal controls. The aircraft's automatic emergency system released a ram air turbine. This was a small propeller powered by the airflow outside the aircraft. It produced just enough hydraulic pressure to let the pilots steer the plane and control its nose position manually.After realising they could not reach Winnipeg, First Officer Quintal suggested landing at the former Royal Canadian Air Force Station Gimli. This was a military airfield where he had trained in the past. The crew did not know that the closed military base had been turned into Gimli Motorsports Park. On the day of the incident, part of the main runway was being used for a sports car event organised by the Winnipeg Sports Car Club. Spectators, campers, and racing cars were parked along the runway. As Captain Pearson, who had years of experience as a glider pilot, brought the aircraft toward Gimli, he realised it was moving too fast and was too high to stop safely on the remaining paved runway. Since both engines had stopped, the crew could not use the wing flaps or slats to slow the aircraft down. Pearson used a forward slip, a rare move for commercial aircraft. It involves using the rudder and aileron controls in opposite directions to turn the aircraft sideways. This increases air resistance and helps the plane lose height quickly without increasing its forward speed. The sideways movement briefly reduced the airflow to the ram air turbine. This made the flight controls harder to operate just before landing. However, Pearson managed to straighten the aircraft in time.The crew lowered the landing gear using a manual gravity release system. The main landing gear locked into position, but the nose gear did not lock properly. The Boeing 767 touched down on the dragstrip section of the airfield. Pearson applied the main wheel brakes, causing two tyres to burst. Two boys riding bicycles on the runway managed to get out of the way as the silent aircraft approached them. Because the nose gear had not locked into place, the front of the aircraft dropped onto the runway. The nose scraped along the concrete, creating a great deal of friction that helped slow down the heavy plane. The front section then hit a steel guardrail installed along the middle of the converted dragstrip. The barrier helped keep the aircraft moving straight along the runway instead of turning toward the spectators. The aircraft came to a complete stop within 3,000 feet of touching down. A small fire near the nose was put out by race track staff using portable fire extinguishers. Passengers left the aircraft using emergency slides. Because the nose had collapsed, the slides hung at steep angles. Some passengers suffered minor cuts, scrapes, and sprains during the evacuation. The Canadian Aviation Safety Board report identified failures in procedures, gaps in staff training, and Air Canada's use of both metric and imperial measurements across its aircraft fleet as main factors behind the incident. The damaged Boeing 767, registered as C-GAUN, was repaired at the Gimli site and returned to commercial service with Air Canada. It continued flying for another 25 years before being retired in 2008.
Article Summary: All 69 people on board survived the incident on 23 July 1983. The fueling mistake happened on the ground in Montreal before the flight departed for Edmonton. The pilots managed to glide the 132-tonne plane for 17 minutes without engine power. They made an emergency landing on a former military runway that had been turned into a sports car race track.
